title: The Sacrifice of the New Creation

content:
Yesterday we looked at the offerings of Numbers 15 and their measurements; the lamb, the ram, and the young bull, each with its grain offering of fine flour and oil and its drink offering of wine. Today let us look into the spiritual meaning of these offerings, and discover what they teach us, the New Creation. For as we study these three animals, we notice something very interesting. Yahweh did not list them randomly. They appear in an ascending order, from the smallest to the largest. First comes the lamb. Then the ram. And finally the young bull. The order itself teaches us an important lesson.

These are not three different ways of approaching God. They reveal increasing depth, increasing cost, and increasing maturity in the worshipper's devotion to Yahweh. And in the same way, the New Creation grows in its understanding and experience of the one perfect sacrifice of Christ. Let us look at each one in turn, and see the journey they describe.

First comes the lamb, and the lamb speaks of the beginning of our walk. The lamb was the most common sacrifice in Israel. It was offered daily upon the altar, and it was the animal that most Israelites could bring. Throughout Scripture, the lamb speaks of innocence, gentleness, and Christ Himself, who is "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). Spiritually, the lamb represents the beginning of the believer's journey. When we first come to Christ, we understand one glorious truth; that we are sinners saved by grace. We believe that Christ died for our sins, we repent, we are baptized, and we begin walking with Him. Peter writes, "Like newborn babies, crave the pure spiritual milk of the word, so that by it you may grow" (1 Peter 2:2). Every New Creation begins as a spiritual infant. There is genuine love for Christ. There is joy in salvation. There is a desire to learn. Yet our understanding is still limited, and like little children, we need continual teaching, correction, and growth.The lamb reminds us that every believer begins as a baby. No one begins with maturity. We all begin simply by trusting the sacrifice of Christ.

Next comes the ram, and the ram speaks of a life of consecration. The ram was more valuable than the lamb, and it was closely connected with consecration. During the ordination of Aaron and his sons, Yahweh commanded that a ram be offered as part of their dedication to priestly service (Exodus 29). And it was a ram that Yahweh provided in place of Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22), revealing His gracious provision. The ram therefore speaks of a believer who has moved beyond simply receiving salvation, and has begun dedicating his entire life to Yahweh. Paul writes, "Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service" (Romans 12:1). As we mature, we discover that the Christian life is not merely about being forgiven. It is about belonging entirely to Christ. Our ambitions become His. Our plans become His. Our time, our possessions, our gifts, and our strength are willingly placed in His hands. This is the life of consecration. The believer no longer asks, "What can Christ do for me?" Instead he asks, "Father, what would You have me to do?" This is the sacrifice of the ram.

Finally comes the young bull, and the young bull speaks of complete maturity. It was the largest and most costly sacrifice mentioned in this chapter. Under the Law, the young bull was offered for the sin of the whole congregation, and also for the high priest himself (Leviticus 4). It represented the greatest offering that an ordinary worshipper could bring. Spiritually, the young bull represents spiritual maturity. The mature believer does not merely understand forgiveness. He does not merely live a consecrated life. He becomes completely yielded to the will of God. Like Paul, he can say, "I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me" (Galatians 2:20). His life is no longer centred upon himself. His greatest desire is to glorify God.

He willingly bears reproach. He endures suffering. He serves others sacrificially. He remains faithful even when obedience is costly. This is not perfection, but maturity. The New Creation has grown from receiving grace to living entirely for the glory of God.

Now we must understand this clearly. The lamb, the ram, and the young bull do not represent three different sacrifices of Christ. There is only one sacrifice; the sacrifice of Christ upon the cross. Rather, these three animals illustrate the believer's growing understanding of, and response to, that one perfect sacrifice. The New Creation journey moves from the lamb, to the ram, to the young bull.
It moves from receiving salvation, to wholehearted consecration, to complete surrender. Paul describes this same growth when he says, "When I was a child, I spoke as a child... but when I became a man, I put away childish things" (1 Corinthians 13:11). And the writer to the Hebrews exhorts believers, "Leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to maturity" (Hebrews 6:1). Yahweh does not desire that His children remain spiritual infants forever. He calls the New Creation to continual growth. Just as a child matures into adulthood, so the believer is called to grow from the simplicity of first faith into complete devotion to Christ.

So, every New Creation begins with the lamb, but Yahweh desires that we continue growing. Our understanding of Christ's one perfect sacrifice should deepen throughout our lives. As we walk with Him, He leads us from salvation to consecration, from consecration to complete surrender, until our greatest desire is no longer simply to receive His blessings, but to glorify Him in every part of our lives. Let us not be content to remain forever at the lamb, precious as that beginning is. Let us press on to the ram of consecration, and then to the bull of complete surrender. May we continue to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ, offering ourselves wholly to God, until the day we stand before the Lamb & God our Father.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,
We thank You that we all began as spiritual infants trusting the Lamb.

But we thank You even more that You do not leave us there.

Lead us on from the lamb of first faith to the ram of a consecrated life.

And lead us on again to the young bull of complete surrender, wholly yielded to Your will.

Let our greatest desire no longer be to receive earthly blessings, but to glorify You in everything.

"But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." - 2 Peter 3:18

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
